To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) experience replay can lead to algorithmic collusion, (b) the collusion is more likely to be formed when the algorithm favors the most recent experience, and (c) the collusion is also more likely when the algorithm is concerned with its relative performance.
(1) Algorithmic collusion is a robust phenomenon that can occur even when algorithms do not communicate with each other.
1) algorithmic collusion still has root in human preferences; 2) randomizing experience can mitigate algorithmic collusion; 3) relative performance concerns can stabilize the collusion.
